title: Struct Packing
prompt:
Write four functions for binary struct packing in `solution.py`:

**Requirements:**
1. `pack_header(version, msg_type, length)` -- packs a 1-byte version, 1-byte message type, and 2-byte length (all unsigned, big-endian) into 4 bytes
2. `unpack_header(data)` -- unpacks 4 bytes into a `(version, msg_type, length)` tuple
3. `pack_point(x, y)` -- packs two floats in little-endian byte order
4. `read_records(data, fmt)` -- a generator that yields tuples by reading consecutive struct-sized chunks from `data`. Skip any trailing bytes that do not fill a complete record

**Examples:**
```python
pack_header(1, 2, 256)              # b'\x01\x02\x01\x00'
unpack_header(b'\x01\x02\x01\x00')  # (1, 2, 256)
pack_point(1.0, 2.0)                # 8 bytes (little-endian floats)
list(read_records(b'\x01\x02\x03\x04', '>HH'))  # [(258, 772)]
```
hints: struct.pack(fmt, ...) converts Python values to bytes
>BBH means big-endian, two unsigned bytes, one unsigned short (2 bytes)
<ff means little-endian, two floats (4 bytes each)
struct.calcsize(fmt) returns the number of bytes for a given format
